scope: Direct reconstruction of the harmonic Schur inertia and equality cases, conditional only on the previously written actual physical zero-support lemma; no new input family or independent review.
block_setup: For sigma=|v><v| in its actual majority eigenbasis, s=sum_i p_i in (0,1), denote the 1111 coordinate z, q=|z|^2, and the remaining vector u. Let A=diag(a_x) for x!=1111, with every a_x>=0 and u_x=0 if a_x=0 by the actual polygon/union argument. Then M(sigma)-I has the exact Hermitian block [[-(1-s)-q,-z u^dagger],[-conj(z) u,A-u u^dagger]]. Its scalar pivot is strictly negative.
schur_and_inertia: Hermitian congruence with the negative pivot gives a direct sum of that pivot and A-c u u^dagger, c=(1-s)/(1-s+q)>0. On ker A the vector u vanishes, so this Schur block splits into an exact zero block and the strictly positive diagonal support. On that support write w=A^{-1/2}u; the remaining block is congruent to I-c ww^dagger, whose only possibly nonunit eigenvalue is 1-c||w||^2. Hence the original matrix has at most one negative eigenvalue iff W=||w||^2<=1/c=1+q/(1-s). Equality W=1/c yields an additional Schur zero eigenvalue, not a negative eigenvalue; strict inequality yields a positive Schur block only if ker A is empty.
physical_spectral_transfer: For pure sigma, M(sigma)>=0 from four actual Schmidt inequalities. The total spinflip identity H1(rho)+tilde rho=4I-M(sigma) reverses the eigenvalue order. Therefore the preceding at-most-one-negative condition on M-I is exactly lambda2(H1(rho)+tilde rho)<=3, including zeros, multiplicities, local phase changes, and all 0<s<1. The separate s>=1 and s=0 cases do not use a singular pivot or W.
precision: This audit does NOT prove W<=1+q/(1-s) for every pure state. If a positive-sector a_x is zero and a physical approximation makes P_x/a_x approach a nonzero constant, the numerical W may jump as in 140, while the matrix eigenvalues remain continuous. No posthoc limiting cancellation is used.
